# L'Independence arabe__disambig_1

'L'Independence arabe' was a monthly political magazine with a special reference to the independence of the Arabs. The magazine was based in Paris, France, and published for one year in the period of 1907–1908.
History and profile
''L'Independence arabe was first published in Paris in April 1907. Naguib Azoury was the director, and Eugène Jung was the editor-in-chief of the magazine which was published on a monthly basis. Azoury published articles in L'Independence arabe which called for the independence of all people living in the Ottoman Empire and for the independent states for them. He argued that France should actively take part in ending the Ottoman oppression against the Arabs. His writings were also anti-Semitic which led to accusations of him being an agent of the Catholic Church.
L'Independence arabe folded after producing 18 issues in September 1908 shortly after the declaration of the constitution in the Ottoman Empire. Because both Azoury and Jung thought that this incident would make the subjects of the Ottomans free. Azoury expressed these views in the final issue of L'Independence arabe''.
